generated_from.requested_focus: Identify a high-impact UX feature that helps users browse and restore prior local conversations without losing the current chat.

evidence.observation: newChat() clears S.messages, writes an empty ff_msgs list, and resets the active chat shell to a blank state.
evidence.relevance: Users currently lose the visible conversation when they start over, so a local archive would solve a real recovery problem.

evidence.observation: Conversation export exists, but it only downloads the current thread as a markdown file and does not offer in-app browsing or restoration.
evidence.relevance: The repo already supports leaving the app with conversation content, but not returning to prior chats inside the product.

evidence.observation: The app already centralizes local and session storage helpers and keeps chat state in a single shared state object.
evidence.relevance: A browser-local history archive can be added without introducing a backend or a new persistence subsystem.

evidence.observation: The UI already has modal patterns for settings and agent management, plus a command palette and focus-aware controls, but no entry point for browsing old chats.
evidence.relevance: The drawer can reuse established dialog and focus patterns while filling a missing product surface.

evidence.observation: The product documentation states that chat history stays local to the browser and that conversation export is available.
evidence.relevance: A local history drawer matches the documented storage model and makes the existing local-only behavior more useful.

evidence.observation: The navigation exposes a single New Chat action, and the empty state assumes one active thread rather than a browsable conversation list.
evidence.relevance: There is no in-app history browser today, so the feature is distinct from the current one-thread workflow.

decision.selection_rationale: Conversation history is the clearest repeated-friction gap in the current single-thread chat flow, and a local drawer can solve it with a focused vertical slice that fits the app's existing browser-only storage model.

candidates.title: Conversation History Drawer
candidates.problem: Users can lose valuable context when they start a new chat because the app has no in-product way to browse or restore prior conversations.
candidates.target_user: People who run multiple chats in the same browser tab and need to revisit earlier answers or context
candidates.measurable_outcome: Increase successful restore actions from archived chats while reducing the need to export or retype prior context.
candidates.vertical_slice: Capture the current conversation when the user starts a new chat, show the latest local threads in a slide-over drawer, and let the user restore one archived chat back into the main view.
candidates.duplication_check: The app can export the active conversation and start a blank chat, but it does not offer an in-app archive or restore path for previous threads.

candidates.title: Composer Draft Autosave
candidates.problem: Users can lose an unsent prompt if they navigate away or start over before sending it.
candidates.target_user: People composing long or interrupted prompts
candidates.measurable_outcome: Reduce lost prompt drafts and retyping after navigation or accidental reset.
candidates.vertical_slice: Persist the current composer text locally and restore it when the chat shell comes back into view.
candidates.duplication_check: The app keeps sent messages locally, but it does not preserve the unsent composer draft.

candidates.title: Search Current Conversation
candidates.problem: Long chats are hard to revisit because users must visually scan the entire message log to find an earlier answer.
candidates.target_user: Users working through long or technical conversations
candidates.measurable_outcome: Reduce time to find a prior answer inside the active chat.
candidates.vertical_slice: Add a text search box that jumps to matching messages in the current thread and highlights the best match.
candidates.duplication_check: The chat view has no in-thread search or jump-to-result behavior.

candidates.title: Last Prompt Resend Shortcut
candidates.problem: Users often want to repeat their last prompt with a small edit, but they must manually copy and re-enter it.
candidates.target_user: Users iterating quickly on a question or instruction
candidates.measurable_outcome: Reduce the number of steps required to resubmit a recent prompt.
candidates.vertical_slice: Add a shortcut and menu action that repopulates the composer with the previous user message for quick editing.
candidates.duplication_check: The app can regenerate an answer from the last message, but it does not surface a user-facing resend shortcut in the composer.

candidates.title: Model Context Hints
candidates.problem: Users can lose track of how much context remains before a conversation needs to be reset.
candidates.measurable_outcome: Reduce surprise resets by making context pressure easier to notice earlier.
candidates.vertical_slice: Show a clearer context indicator with an optional explain-this-state hint near the chat header.
candidates.duplication_check: The app already has a context pill, so this is an explanation refinement rather than a new capability.

candidates.title: Agent Starter Chips
candidates.problem: Users starting a new chat with a custom agent may need a faster way to launch a first prompt that matches the agent's purpose.
candidates.target_user: Users who rely on saved agents as starting points
candidates.measurable_outcome: Increase first-message sends from the empty state.
candidates.vertical_slice: Show a small, agent-aware set of starter prompt chips in the empty state and fall back to the current defaults when none exist.
candidates.duplication_check: The empty state already has starter prompts, but they are static and not tailored to the active agent.

problem.statement: When users start a new chat, the current conversation disappears from the main UI and there is no in-product way to browse or restore prior threads, so useful context is easy to lose even though the app already keeps chat history local to the browser.
affected_users: People who run multiple conversations in one browser tab
Users who want to revisit prior answers or prompts
Users who prefer to keep working without exporting files
jobs_to_be_done: Reopen a previous conversation without reconstructing it manually
Move between current and earlier chats without leaving the app
Preserve useful context before starting a fresh thread
current_friction: newChat() clears the active thread from the visible chat shell
Export exists, but it takes the user out of the in-app flow instead of letting them restore the content
The main navigation exposes only a blank-thread action, not a way to browse archived chats

outcomes.user_value: Users can recover prior chats in place instead of retyping or exporting them, which makes the app more useful for iterative work.
outcomes.product_value: The app gains continuity and session recovery without changing its browser-local storage model or introducing server-side history.

metrics.name: History restore success rate
metrics.definition: Successful restore actions divided by history drawer open actions.
metrics.target: Increase after rollout while keeping false restores low
metrics.instrumentation: Emit conversation_history_drawer_opened and conversation_history_restored from freeforge/src/features/history.js; aggregate the ratio over the review window.
metrics.guardrail: Do not count restores that replace the wrong snapshot or drop unsent user input.

metrics.name: Time to reopen a prior thread
metrics.definition: Median seconds from opening the history drawer to restoring a previous conversation.
metrics.target: Decrease or stay flat while restore success rises
metrics.instrumentation: Use the same history drawer events plus a browser timing mark in the restore path.
metrics.guardrail: Do not reduce time by hiding confirmation when current text would be replaced.

metrics.name: Unintended overwrite incidents
metrics.definition: Count of verified cases where restoring history overwrote unsent composer text or the wrong archived chat.
metrics.instrumentation: QA notes, local error logs, and manual verification of restore confirmations.
metrics.guardrail: Any confirmed increase is a rollback candidate.

scope.mvp: Capture recent local conversations before starting a new chat, show them in a slide-over history drawer, and restore one archived thread into the main chat shell.
in_scope: Persist a capped list of local conversation snapshots
Show each snapshot with a short preview, timestamp, and model or agent metadata
Restore an archived conversation into the chat shell
Warn before replacing unsent composer text with a restored thread
non_goals: Search, tagging, or pinning archived chats
Per-thread deletion or bulk history management
Redesigning export beyond the current download flow
assumptions: Local browser storage is sufficient for a capped archive of recent chats
The app can restore a snapshot into the current chat shell without a backend round trip
The existing modal and focus patterns are enough to support a drawer-style history surface
constraints: Keep conversation history browser-local and do not send message content to analytics
Cap retained snapshots so the drawer does not grow without bound
Preserve the current chat until the user explicitly confirms a restore that would replace unsent text
Keep restore behavior compatible with the active model and agent context

entry_points: New Chat button in the top navigation
History button added near the existing navigation actions

primary_flow.action: Opens the history drawer from the chat shell.
primary_flow.system_response: The drawer slides in with the most recent archived conversations listed first and the current thread clearly labeled.
primary_flow.success_condition: The user can scan recent chats without losing the active conversation.

primary_flow.action: Selects an archived conversation to restore.
primary_flow.system_response: The app warns if unsent composer text would be replaced, then swaps the main chat shell to the selected snapshot and closes the drawer on confirmation.
primary_flow.success_condition: The restored conversation becomes the active thread with the right model and agent context.

primary_flow.action: Returns to the drawer later and picks a different thread.
primary_flow.system_response: The app restores the second snapshot in the same way, keeping the browser-local archive intact.
primary_flow.success_condition: The user can move between prior chats without exporting files or rebuilding context.

alternate_flows.name: Empty history
steps: Show an empty state with guidance to send a message first
alternate_flows.resolution: The user understands that there is nothing to restore yet.

alternate_flows.name: Cancel restore
alternate_flows.trigger: The user backs out of a restore that would replace unsent text.
steps: Allow cancel without changing the active thread
Keep the unsent text in the composer
alternate_flows.resolution: No content is lost unless the user confirms the replacement.

states.trigger: The drawer is closed and the current chat is active.
states.experience: Show the normal chat shell with no archive overlay.
states.recovery: No recovery is needed until the user opens history or starts a restore.

states.not_applicable_reason: History snapshots are read synchronously from browser storage, so the MVP does not need a remote loading state.

states.trigger: The user confirms a restore and the selected snapshot becomes the active thread.
states.experience: Close the drawer, render the restored messages, and announce that the archived chat is active again.
states.recovery: No recovery is needed unless the user wants to switch to a different archived thread.

states.experience: Show a short explanation that history will appear after the user sends a chat.
states.recovery: The user can close the drawer and start the first conversation.

states.trigger: A stored snapshot cannot be read, the archive is corrupted, or browser storage fails while saving a history entry.
states.experience: Show a readable error and keep the active chat usable even if the archive list is partially unavailable.
states.recovery: The user can dismiss the error, continue chatting, and the app can fall back to the remaining readable snapshots.

states.not_applicable_reason: The MVP does not add a permission gate; archive access is local to the browser and does not depend on a separate permission model.
Conversation history is browser-local and does not require a sign-in state or token refresh path.
The drawer reads local storage and does not need network connectivity to function.
Restoring a snapshot is atomic for the MVP; the app either swaps to the archived thread or leaves the current chat untouched.
The restore path does not rely on a long-lived remote request, so interruption only closes the drawer or browser without a resumable transfer.

states.trigger: The user closes the drawer or backs out of the replace confirmation.
states.experience: Dismiss the drawer and preserve the current chat and unsent composer text.
states.recovery: The user can reopen history later and choose a different thread.

states.trigger: The current composer contains unsent text or the active chat has diverged from the archived snapshot the user wants to restore.
states.experience: Warn that restoring will replace the current draft and show the age of the selected archive item.
states.recovery: The user can cancel the restore or confirm the replacement and continue from the archived thread.

accessibility.requirement: Opening the drawer moves focus into the drawer, tab order stays predictable, Escape closes the surface, and focus returns to the opener after close or restore.
accessibility.verification: Use the keyboard only to open history, select a thread, cancel a replace warning, and close the drawer.

accessibility.requirement: Empty state, restore success, replace warnings, and storage errors are announced through readable text or live regions rather than color alone.
accessibility.verification: Run the drawer flow with a screen reader and confirm the selected thread and state changes are spoken clearly.

accessibility.requirement: Each history item shows a short preview, timestamp, and metadata chip so the user can identify a thread without relying on hidden context.
accessibility.verification: Inspect the drawer in normal, high-contrast, and grayscale rendering.

accessibility.requirement: Drawer animations respect reduced-motion preferences and interactive targets stay usable on narrow touch screens.
accessibility.verification: Enable reduced motion and test the drawer on a mobile-width viewport.

content_guidance: Use the first user prompt as the item label and keep the preview short.
Show a simple timestamp and model or agent metadata for orientation.
If a restore would replace unsent text, say that explicitly before the confirmation action.
Do not surface raw message content in analytics or error copy beyond the intentionally visible preview.
user_controls: Open and close the history drawer
Cancel a restore that would replace unsent text
Return to the current chat without changing the archive

implementation.architecture_fit: Add a browser-local conversation archive alongside the existing single-thread chat state, reusing the current storage helpers and dialog/focus patterns instead of introducing a server-backed history system.

work_items.title: Capture and store conversation snapshots
work_items.objective: Persist a capped local archive whenever the user starts a new chat or completes a conversation turn that should be restorable later.

paths.rationale: Capture the current thread before newChat() clears it and keep the active chat state in sync with the archive.
Add any small storage helpers or state fields needed for the local archive metadata.
Centralize archive snapshot, list, prune, and restore helpers for the drawer.

instructions: Store only the data needed to recreate a conversation thread, including messages and the active model or agent context.
Cap the archive so it cannot grow without bound and prune the oldest entries first.
Keep the current chat visible until the archive write succeeds.
Do not change the existing message rendering or export behavior while wiring the archive.
done_when: Starting a new chat preserves a restorable snapshot of the prior thread.
Reloading the page still shows the capped local archive.
The archive never stores more than the configured number of snapshots.

work_items.title: Build the history drawer surface
work_items.objective: Give users a browsable slide-over list of archived conversations with an obvious entry point from the main navigation.

paths.rationale: Add the drawer markup and the History entry point near the existing chat actions.
Render the archive list, empty state, and restore controls.
Wire the new History trigger and drawer close behavior into the app bootstrap.

instructions: Use the existing dialog and focus patterns so the drawer behaves consistently with the settings and agent surfaces.
Show the most recent archived thread first with a short preview and timestamp.
Include a clear empty state and an obvious close action.
Do not add search or per-thread deletion in the MVP.
done_when: The drawer opens from the main navigation and lists archived threads.
The empty state is understandable when no history exists.
Keyboard users can enter and exit the drawer without losing their place.

work_items.title: Restore archived chats safely
work_items.objective: Replace the current thread with a selected archived snapshot only after explicit user confirmation when unsent text would be lost.

paths.rationale: Apply the restored snapshot to the main chat shell and reset transient streaming or undo state.
Wire the restore entry point, confirmation flow, and drawer close behavior into the app bootstrap.

instructions: The drawer UI should already exist from work-02; this work only wires the restore path into the live chat shell.
Restore messages, context metadata, and the active model or agent context together.
If the composer contains unsent text, warn before replacing it and preserve the draft when the user cancels.
Return focus to the composer or the control that opened the drawer after a successful restore.
Keep restore behavior deterministic so repeated opens show the same archived snapshot ordering.
done_when: Selecting an archived thread replaces the current chat with the correct snapshot.
Cancelling a replace warning preserves the current draft.
The drawer closes and focus is restored after a successful restore.

work_items.title: Lock down history behavior with tests
work_items.objective: Prove archive creation, drawer browsing, safe restore, and accessibility behavior with browser-level coverage.

paths.rationale: Cover the drawer open, empty, restore, and focus-restoration flows.
Add wiring coverage for snapshot capture and restore state transitions if needed.

instructions: Add a test that confirms new chat archives the current thread before clearing it.
Cover opening the drawer, restoring a snapshot, and canceling a replace warning.
Verify keyboard-only focus restoration and the empty history state.
Assert that no test path requires network access to open archived conversations.
done_when: The updated tests fail before the feature and pass after it.
The suite proves archive capture, restore, and cancellation are stable.
Accessibility regressions around focus and empty state are covered.

data_changes: Add a capped browser-local archive of conversation snapshots keyed by the current user session.
Keep the existing current-thread storage in place so the app still has a single live conversation view.
Store only the metadata needed to recreate the thread, not analytics payloads or unrelated browser state.
api_changes: No public API change is required for the MVP.
All history behavior stays inside the client and browser storage layer.

analytics_events.name: conversation_history_drawer_opened
analytics_events.trigger: The user opens the history drawer from the chat shell.
analytics_events.purpose: Measure how often users look for prior chats and whether they have a restore conflict.

analytics_events.name: conversation_history_restore_requested
analytics_events.trigger: The user selects an archived chat and reaches the restore confirmation step.
analytics_events.purpose: Track restore intent without recording message content.

analytics_events.name: conversation_history_restored
analytics_events.trigger: An archived conversation becomes the active chat shell.
analytics_events.purpose: Measure successful restoration and thread reuse.

security_privacy: Keep history local to the browser and never upload message content as part of this feature.
Cap the retained archive so the feature does not accumulate unnecessary sensitive text indefinitely.
Do not include raw message content in analytics or toast text.
Preserve the current unsent draft unless the user explicitly confirms replacement.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user has at least one archived conversation
acceptance_criteria.then: The drawer shows the most recent archive first, exposes a clear way to restore it, and places focus inside the drawer
acceptance_criteria.verification: Automated drawer-open test plus manual keyboard smoke test

acceptance_criteria.given: A user selects an archived conversation with no unsent text in the composer
acceptance_criteria.then: The current chat shell shows the archived messages and the drawer closes after restoring focus

acceptance_criteria.given: A user has unsent text in the composer
acceptance_criteria.when: They attempt to restore a different archived conversation
acceptance_criteria.then: The app warns that the current draft will be replaced, and cancelling the warning preserves the draft

acceptance_criteria.when: The user opens the history drawer
acceptance_criteria.then: The drawer shows an empty state instead of broken controls, and the user can close it without side effects

unit: Test archive snapshot creation and pruning behavior.
Test archive item labeling from the first user message and metadata.
integration: Test opening the history drawer and restoring a saved thread.
Test the replace warning when unsent composer text is present.
end_to_end: Start a conversation, archive it through New Chat, and restore it from history.
Open history with no saved threads and confirm the empty state path.
accessibility: Verify keyboard-only drawer open, restore, cancel, and close behavior.
Verify live announcements and reduced-motion behavior.
manual: Check the drawer on a narrow mobile viewport.
Confirm that the archive preview does not expose more content than intended.

phases: Enable locally for test runs and verify snapshot capture.
Ship to internal usage after keyboard and restore tests pass.
Turn on by default once storage quota and restore behavior are stable.
rollback_triggers: Restoring a thread overwrites the wrong chat
Archive writes exceed local storage quotas too often
Focus is lost when opening or closing the history drawer
rollback_plan: Leave the current New Chat flow intact while removing the archive drawer wiring.
Keep the existing export action available as the fallback for preserving conversations.
observability: Track drawer opens, successful restores, empty-state views, and storage failures.
Watch for QA notes about wrong-thread restoration or lost unsent text.
Review browser storage quota warnings if the archive grows too quickly.

risks.risk: Storing recent chats locally could push the browser toward storage limits sooner than the current single-thread model.
risks.mitigation: Cap the archive, prune oldest entries first, and keep snapshots minimal.

risks.risk: A restore action could overwrite unsent composer text if the warning is too subtle.
risks.mitigation: Require an explicit replace confirmation whenever the current draft would be lost.

risks.risk: Archived previews could expose more conversation content than users expect on a shared screen.
risks.mitigation: Keep previews short, show only the first prompt and metadata, and avoid raw analytics capture.

stop_conditions: Stop if the archive cannot be persisted without exposing message content outside the browser-local storage model.
Stop if restoring a snapshot would break the existing model or agent context boundaries.
Stop if the drawer cannot reuse the current dialog and focus behavior without introducing accessibility regressions.
Stop if validation fails or the history snapshot tests become flaky.
completion_evidence: Passing browser-level tests for archive capture, drawer browsing, restore, and cancel flows
Passing lint and test commands for the app and security suites
Manual keyboard smoke test showing the drawer opens, restores, and returns focus correctly
No raw conversation content exposed in analytics, toasts, or error copy
